answers.stem_only: Replace the cache policy with one whose cache key holds only the lang query string (no cookies, no headers), which is configuration and not code; and turn on Origin Shield in the Region closest to the origin so that requests from the many edge locations collapse into one caching layer before the EC2 origin.

Restrict the ALB security group to the AWS-managed prefix list for CloudFront origin-facing addresses (no IP-range maintenance), and have CloudFront add a secret custom origin header that an ALB listener rule requires (forward only when the header matches, default action returns 403), so that other customers' distributions cannot reach the application.

Add a second endpoint group for us-west-2 on the same listener with the us-west-2 NLB as its endpoint, and set that group's traffic dial to 0 percent (us-east-1 at 100 percent); Global Accelerator health checks then fail traffic over to the us-west-2 group only when the us-east-1 endpoints are unhealthy.

Use origin access control (OAC) on the S3 origin, allow PUT and the other methods in the cache behavior, and grant the CloudFront service principal (conditioned on the distribution ARN) access in the bucket policy and kms:Decrypt/Encrypt/GenerateDataKey in the KMS key policy; OAI does not support SSE-KMS, and the bucket stays private with Block Public Access on.

The patch files are static, identical for all players and change weekly, so cache them at the edge: put an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the existing load balancers (or an S3 origin) so far-away players download from a nearby edge location; Global Accelerator only speeds the network path and still serves every byte from the Region.
